en: Dhṛṣṭi, bhuvana, aṃśu, nābhi, viṣṇapāt, ādada, etam, pratna, indra, it, kṣatrasya, indrasya, mitra, asi, agne, yannavate, yaḥ, vā, ayathādevatam, sphya, svasti, agniḥ, bhūtānām, āpyāyasva, mā, chandaḥ, īyuḥ, kramaiḥ, ghnanti, somaḥ, vai, bhuvaḥ, devānām, utsṛjyām, iti, ekaikaḥ; ayam, vām, prātaryujā, vayam, venaḥ, triṃśat, trayaḥ, mūrddhānam, indrāgnī.

Oṃ! This month [belongs] to Indra accompanied by the Maruts; Indra accompanied by the Maruts, the great one, has eaten with the great unobstructed ones. O Agni, [give] the golden-handed one; [give] the lifespans. Arise, O charioteer; stand firm. You are the great one of all. May the well-disposed Agni [grant] joy. Let it swell for the sake of the immortal. Kindling him, [he is] the support of the great ones. By means of Agni, the god, this one—Puruharikeśa—with Agni and Viṣṇu, well-disposed, for the sake of the heavenly world. The thunderbolt is united. Of the god, he has given this. They have seized this [earth]. He who gives breath, he who gives the self. These are the paths, two by two. 2.

For long life; may the waters flow toward you; you are the one who sits near; I pour you out; O divine waters, you are the encompassers; the conqueror of the earth; in you is the power of Indra and Agni; may the three gods not cause you to waver; let the divine ones kindle you; for the heart, O Soma, I take you; first for Vāyu, for Agni Nīkavata; what has come newly; three indeed; O divine Savitṛ; this belongs to Vāstoṣpati; of Indra, the protector of the body; O Agni, I take it into myself; four, four. 4 The former is firm; for every man; the brilliance of Soma; the former belongs to the Maruts; O Agni, of those born; the cups; the steed; five, five. 5

First for the earth, first for the sacrificial grass—*svāhā*. May the two of us, O Agni, [attain] six by six. (6) They yoke me at any time to strength. Verily, the gods [are] two by two; may the two of us [attain] seven by seven. (7) The burning away, that rising one—we have gone to the former. You are taken with a support; [you are] for the man-seated [deity]. To Indra and Agni, [an offering] on eleven potsherds; to the Maruts. May the Vasus pull you forth. Full behind, I offer the consciousness; becoming bliss, the wind—eight by eight. (8)
For wide indeed is the domain of Savitar; may he protect us. Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ—nine times nine (ninety-nine). 9.
This youth, may Sūrya protect him—ten times ten (one hundred). 10.

O Agni, favored with cattle and with speech, grant us long life. O Agni, may the Vasus accept your oblation. May they establish you as one whose dwelling is firm. The Gāyatrī meter has three feet. Who fashions you? What indeed was there in the beginning? Eleven times eleven (one hundred and twenty-one). 11.
Dhātṛ, Ārti, Sūrya, and the god [Agni]—thousands upon thousands, twelve by twelve (12). Those gods who are the destroyers of sacrifice, thirteen (13).
This impulsion of strength, fourteen (14).
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, for Soma accompanied by the Pitṛs, O divine Agni, turn hither; the sacrifice is complete—fifteen (15).
For indeed, Vāja is our food—seventeen, sixteen, sixteen (16).
Intention has mounted upon Agni—all, thee, O Agni, the bull—seventeen, seventeen (17).
The one who yokes [the sacrifice] with eighteen (18) names; the measure of the day is Mitra; those who anoint the prize-winning steed when kindled, twenty-one (21), twenty-one (21);
Vāyu is present with his splendor; Viṣṇu’s stride is in the waters; the Soma-juice for Indra—twenty-three (23).
He who [praises] you with a humble heart; may the mind not harm you in the dwelling-place of the divine Earth—these are twenty-four.
I behold your former life-span; when you cried out—these are twenty-five.
Being born from Prajāpati, I yoke Agni; golden-hued and pure—these are twenty-six.
Both of you, O Indra and Agni, as we approach—new and ever new—is that which, O Agni, are the twenty-seven [verses].
With the kindled [fire], the quarters first; him upward, the northern, twenty-eight.
Day by day, the months first; O Lord of Food, give us food—Yama, dwelling in wealth, sharpening his vigor, the bull, twenty-nine.
Salutations to you, O Rudra, in the eastern direction; thirty (30) [deities]. To the south-eastern sacrifice, thirty-one (31).
O Amba, O Ambali, thirty-two (32).
Desiring you at the invocation, [the verse] "ūrjam" (strength), these thirty-three;
in Agni and Viṣṇu, the great, thirty-four;
perform your vigor, "imām agr̥bṇan raśanām" (they grasped this rein), thirty-five.

May Vaiśvānara come to us with his aid. Indra for you, the peerless one from every side; Indra, O heroes, as of old, with a newer song. This is your seat, O Agni—I meditate upon it. Thirty-six. 36. We invoke Indra for you first;
thirty-seven. 37. Yoke your horses, indeed; thirty-eight. 38.
O Agni, you are the great and lofty; his fuel-sticks are kindled; the plants are firm; you are the supporter, the foundation—like a cloud [there are] thirty-nine (39).
[There are] forty (40) when added together;
[there are] forty-one (41) for the god, O goddess.
*hiraṇyagarbha āpaḥ* (Hiraṇyagarbha, the waters) has forty-eight [verses];
*agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat* (Agni, slaying the Vṛtras) has fifty-four;
*tvam agne rudraḥ* (You, O Agni, are Rudra) has fifty-five.
"By Agni, wealth"—fifty-seven (57).
"Agni is the head of heaven"—fifty-nine (59).
The indication of the end is completed.
